title: AI-Based Detection of Cyber Threats in Unidirectional IP Traffic
dataset_link:
a)Synthetic and lab-generated traffic: Benign load from iperf3, Ostinato, or TRex; attack traffic from hping3 (SYN/UDP floods), Slowloris (slow HTTP exhaustion), dnscat2/iodine (DNS tunnelling), and DGA samples from published algorithms (e.g., via DGArchive) or a sandboxed C2 emulator for realistic beaconing timing.

b)Feature extraction : Extrac
description:
• Background Critical-infrastructure operators observe their gateway and peering links using passive mirroring or hardware data diodes that copy traffic into a monitoring enclave in one direction only. The enclave can see everything crossing the link, but it has no physical or protocol-level path back into the production network. This is deliberate as it removes an entire class of attack in which a compromised monitoring or analytics system becomes a pivot into the core network, and it preserves a clean chain of custody for forensic use. The trade-off is that any intelligence layer sitting in that enclave must work purely from what it can passively observe such as packet captures, exported flow records (NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow), and derived metadata with no ability to send probes, complete handshakes with the traffic source, or push a mitigation command back.
• Description The objective is to design and build an AI/ML pipeline that ingests a one-directional stream of IP traffic from a simulated IP data and detects, classifies, and scores cyber-security threats in near real time, using only passively collected data. The pipeline must assume it can never re-contact the traffic's source or destination, cannot rely on completing any handshake itself, and cannot issue any action back across the ingest path. Its output is intelligence as labelled alerts, confidence scores, and supporting evidence displayed on visualisation dashboard. The system is designed to detect the following types of threat:
a. Volumetric / protocol DDoS: SYN floods, UDP reflection/amplification, and spoofed-source floods identified from flow-level rate and source-IP entropy statistics.
b. Botnet C2 beaconing: Periodicity and inter-arrival analysis on flows that repeat at regular intervals toward a small set of destinations.
c. DGA domains and DNS tunnelling: Entropy/n-gram analysis of DNS query names, plus query-length and record-type anomalies.
d. Malware inside encrypted sessions: Detection from TLS/QUIC metadata alone (JA3/JA3S or JA4 fingerprints, packet-size and timing sequences), without decrypting payload.
e. Reconnaissance and port scanning: Fan-out patterns from a single source across many destination ports or hosts.
f. Data exfiltration: Asymmetric flow-volume anomalies and unusual outbound-to-inbound byte ratios.
Expected Solution The system must be delivered as working prototype (source repository) implementing ingest, feature extraction, model inference, and alert output. Accompanying documentation of the model(s) used, features engineered, and the training/validation approach. The prototype must also include a simple dashboard of live or replayed detections with severity and confidence adhering to the following architectural constraints:
a. Read-only ingest: Treat the input as strictly read-only. Any design that assumes a return path, a live query to the source, or an inline block is out of scope.
b. No payload decryption: TLS/QUIC sessions must be analysed from metadata only, never from decrypted content.
c. Streaming, not batch: The pipeline must process traffic incrementally and raise alerts with bounded latency, not just produce an end-of-run report.
d. Defined throughput target: Solutions must state and demonstrate the traffic rate they were tested against (e.g., flows/sec or Mbps sustained).
e. Standardized alert schema: Alerts must be structured records for instance timestamp, flow identifier, threat class, confidence score, and supporting evidence feature.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, ml applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on model, protocol, infrastructure. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 19/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI-Based Detection of Cyber Threats in Unidirectional IP Traffic

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an AI system that can spot cyberattacks by only watching network traffic flow one way, through a data diode, with no ability to send probes or get responses back, exactly how critical infrastructure security monitoring actually works.
overview.why_it_matters: Data diodes are used specifically because they prevent a compromised monitoring system from becoming an attack pathway back into critical infrastructure. A detection system that respects this one-way constraint is what actually deploys in these real, high-security environments.
pain_points: Any intelligence layer in a one-way monitoring enclave can only passively observe, never probe or interact.
Traditional active security tools (that complete handshakes, send probes) don't work in this constraint.
Detecting sophisticated threats from passive observation alone (packet captures, flow records) is genuinely harder than active monitoring.
overview.background: Critical infrastructure operators use one-way data diodes for security monitoring specifically to prevent the monitoring system itself from becoming an attack pivot, but this means any AI detection layer must work purely from passive observation.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI/ML pipeline detecting, classifying, and scoring cyber threats in near real time from a simulated one-directional IP traffic stream, using only passively collected data (packet captures, flow records, metadata).
expected_solution: AI/ML-based threat detection, classification, and scoring.
Near-real-time processing suitable for the one-way constraint.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Designing detection specifically constrained to passive-only observation (no active probing, no response capability) is a real, meaningful constraint that shapes the entire technical approach, genuine domain sophistication.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires real network traffic analysis and ML feature engineering under a genuine architectural constraint, substantial technical depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine network security and ML expertise together, specifically understanding the passive-only constraint's implications.

innovation.note: Genuine passive-only detection constraint (no active probing capability) shapes real, meaningful technical sophistication.

invention.note: Feature engineering from passive network telemetry alone, without active enrichment, is genuinely harder than typical network security ML.

technical_feasibility.note: Simulated IP traffic can be constructed or public network traffic datasets used; the passive-only constraint is a design principle, not a data-access barrier.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly applicable to real critical infrastructure security architectures.

architecture.note: A passive-observation-only ML pipeline, well-understood pattern with a genuine architectural constraint shaping design.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with network security ML experience. The passive-only constraint is the actual technical differentiator, design your entire pipeline around never needing active interaction, that's what makes this genuinely relevant to real data-diode-protected environments.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-articulated, real architectural constraint (genuinely one-way, no active capability) that shapes meaningful technical design decisions.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a detection system that implicitly assumes active capability (e.g. features that would require response/interaction) would violate the core constraint this PS is specifically testing for.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Design every feature and detection technique to work purely from passive observation, no assumption of active probing, handshake completion, or response capability anywhere in your pipeline.

idea_0_4: Source or construct simulated IP traffic data representing passive network observation (packet captures, flow records).
Design your feature set explicitly limited to what's passively observable, no active-probing-dependent features.
Split: one person on traffic ingestion/feature engineering, one on the detection/classification model.
prototype_4_22: Build your passive traffic ingestion and feature-extraction pipeline.
Build your AI/ML threat-detection and classification model.
Start scoring/prioritization logic for detected threats.
integration_22_30: Connect ingestion, detection, and scoring into one coherent near-real-time pipeline.
Test against simulated attack traffic patterns embedded in your test data.
Add explainability output for detected threats.
polish_30_36: Build a clear analyst-facing dashboard showing detected/scored threats with explainable reasoning.
Rehearse explaining how your entire pipeline respects the passive-only constraint explicitly.
Prepare to discuss detection accuracy and false-positive tradeoffs.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Explicitly walk through why your specific feature choices work under the passive-only constraint, contrasting with what an active-monitoring system could additionally do, that genuine understanding of the constraint's implications is the real technical substance here.

strengths: Very well-articulated, real architectural constraint shapes genuine technical sophistication.
Directly applicable to real critical infrastructure security deployments.
weaknesses: Passive-only detection is genuinely harder than active monitoring, inherent accuracy tradeoffs.
Real critical-infrastructure traffic data isn't accessible, simulated data quality matters.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, with real understanding of the passive-only architectural constraint shared across the team.
team_fit.approach: Design your feature set around the passive-only constraint from hour 0, this shapes everything downstream.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing features and detection logic that genuinely respect the passive-only constraint, that requires real network security domain understanding.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded detection system that implicitly assumes active capability would fail the actual real-world deployment constraint this PS is testing for.

data_resource_availability.status: Simulated IP traffic data is the appropriate approach given real critical infrastructure traffic isn't accessible.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct realistic simulated traffic with embedded attack patterns, clearly labeled as simulated.

judge_qna.question: How does your system avoid relying on active probing or response capability anywhere in the pipeline?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific feature set and confirm each is derivable purely from passive observation, no handshake completion or probe response anywhere.
judge_qna.follow_up: What detection capability would you lose entirely without any active probing ability, and how do you compensate?

judge_qna.question: How does your detection accuracy compare to what an active-monitoring system could achieve?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about the inherent tradeoff, passive-only detection has real limitations compared to active monitoring, describe what your system gains in return (deployment safety, no pivot risk).
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your false-negative rate for threats that would be more easily caught with active interaction?
